extracted.intended_audience: journalism students, society editors, and newspaper reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing society (personal/social) newspaper items: form, style, and editorial choices for reporting marriages, engagements, romances and other social events. Emphasizes variety, tone, and adherence to social usage and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and style determined by social usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The form and style suitable to such news are partly determined by social usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Society copy should follow conventions of the social milieu being reported; typographical and stylistic choices may differ from other newspaper sections because of these usages. Consider customary expectations of the community when choosing tone, level of detail, and formality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style may differ from other sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The typographical style of the society columns often differs somewhat from that of other parts of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and writers should be aware that society pages commonly use different typographical conventions (headings, ordering of personal names, presentation of events) and may format items (announcements, brief notices, descriptive paragraphs) distinctively to suit readers of the society section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give variety; avoid stock phrases and trite description
rubrics_metrics.description: Society news taxes the writer's ability to give variety to stories of the same kind of events as they take place day by day. In no other kind of news is he more frequently tempted to use stock phrases over and over again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consciously vary phrasing, leads, and angle when covering repeated event types (weddings, engagements, parties). Strive to avoid cliché and colorless description; seek fresh detail, different narrative angles, and vivid but tasteful language to keep recurring items engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat unusual courtships/engagements/weddings as regular news when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual courtships, engagements, and weddings may be treated as regular news; in that case the stories of them are not often placed in the society section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a social event has broader interest or newsworthiness (novelty, public figure involved, unusual circumstances), consider writing it as straight news rather than a society item and place it accordingly. Use journalistic news conventions (lead emphasizing the news angle) for such pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop humorous or pathetic possibilities without violating good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Such news not infrequently has humorous and pathetic possibilities that the writer may develop without violating the canons of good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may exploit human-interest, humor, or pathos in social stories but must balance appeal with propriety. Avoid sensationalizing private grief or ridiculing subjects; maintain respect for persons while shaping narrative interest.
